About the course
Curriculum planning
The graduate program in the Structural Engineering Division of the Department of Civil Engineering offers comprehensive courses on Earthquake Engineering, including Structural Dynamics, Seismic Analysis and Design of Structures, Behavior of Reinforced Concrete Structures, Seismic Design of Steel Structures, and (Passive and Active) Structural Control. The courses are given in English.
The Structural Engineering Division collaborates closely with the world-famous research center on earthquake engineering, the National Center for Research on Earthquake Engineering (also known as NCREE, see www.ncree.org for more information) in Taiwan, to conduct research on the following topics:
a) seismic hazard analysis,
b) seismic behavior of structural and non-structural components,
c) seismic analysis, design and retrofit of structures,
d) system identification and structural health monitoring,
e) passive and active structural control, and
f) seismic performance-based design.
The collaboration with NCREE also provides graduate students with opportunities to conduct large-scale dynamic, pseudodynamic, and quasistatic tests.
Program Duration: 2 to 7 years, with 24 credits in total as a requirement for graduation.
Required Courses include Academic Ethics, Ph.D. Dissertation, Seminar on Structural Engineering (4 semesters), and courses required by the advisor. Credits for dissertation and seminars do not count towards the graduation requirement.

Career options
The graduates are trained to work in the professional fields of structural engineering, architectural engineering, hydraulic engineering, soil engineering, transportation engineering, spatial information surveying, land administration, and survey mapping offered by government units, private enterprises, and research institutes.
Qualifications
Civil engineer, structural engineer, architect, geotechnical engineer, hydraulic engineer, environmental engineer, traffic engineer, survey engineer, urban planning engineer, refrigeration air-conditioning engineer, industrial safety engineer, industrial hygiene engineer, mining safety engineer.

Introduction
The Department of Civil Engineering of National Taiwan University was established in 1945. It offers both undergraduate and graduate programs. It is recognized as the largest and leading one among all civil engineering departments in the nation.
The Department partakes in numerous national infrastructure projects and has a well-established education and research reputation spanning from its specialized engineering fields in Geotechnical, Structural, Hydraulic, Transportation, Computer-Aided, Construction Management, Surveying & Geospatial, and AI for Engineering Applications. It also establishes a close-knit network with the government, academia, and industries and promotes crossover collaboration.
Internationally, the Department is accredited by the Washington Accord, ranked 49 in the 2026 QS World University Rankings by Subject in Civil and Structural Engineering, and offers English-taught programs for undergraduate and graduate degrees.

Application documents
Passport or ID
[Details]
Please provide a scanned copy of your passport; if you don't have a passport, please upload any national ID with your name on it such as ID card, driver's license, etc., that clearly indicates your full name and nationality.
Alien Resident Certificate (ARC) (if applicable)
[Details]
If you are a current or past holder of an ARC in Taiwan, please upload a copy here.
Graduation Certificate of highest degree awarded - Original version
[Details]
Please submit an official Graduation Certificate issued by the school/university. Students graduating in the current year shall submit a Certificate of Expected Graduation or a Certificate of Enrollment officially issued by the school/university.
Full Transcript of highest degree awarded (including records of each year and explanation of grading system) - Original version
[Details]
High school graduates must submit academic transcripts for grades 10 to 12. Graduates whose graduating year is academically equivalent to the second grade of a senior secondary school in Taiwan of a comparable academic level and nature, must submit transcripts for grades 7 to 11.
Graduation Certificate of highest degree awarded - Translated version
[Details]
Translated version is required if the original one is not in Chinese or English.
Full Transcript of highest degree awarded (including records of each year and explanation of grading system) - Translated version
[Details]
Translated version is required if the original one is not in Chinese or English.
Financial Statement
[Details]
All applicants shall provide a bank statement, issued by a bank within the past 3 months, showing a minimum balance equivalent to NTD 200,000 in savings deposit.
Scholarship recipients shall provide proof of scholarship. Applicants who have been granted scholarships or assistantships by NTU professors or departments/graduate institutes may submit relevant proof instead of a bank statement.
*If the bank account is not under the applicant's name, please submit the bank statement and the financial supporter's signed guarantee of financial support.
*If an applicant's bank account statement has insufficient funds, please submit the applicant's and financial supporter's bank statements with the total savings equivalent to NTD 200,000 within 3 months. Besides, the financial supporter shall also provide his or her signed guarantee of financial support.

[Details]
An autobiography written either in Chinese or English, with no limit to the number of words.

[Details]

[Details]

[Details]
Should you wish to apply for the scholarship, please explain, in less than 500 words, why you are more preferable to receive the scholarship.

None

None
Additional notes
Although you do not need an advisor's confirmation to apply to NTU, you are encouraged to contact professors whom you are genuinely interested in working with to discuss your research direction and may reflect the discussion results in your "Research Proposal."
Please visit our Department's website for our faculty research expertise. Confirmation of your advisor comes after being admitted to NTU.
Scholarship from college or department
Name : NTUCE PhD Student Scholarship
Amount : (PhD) NTD 240,000 (≈USD 8,000) for 1 year
Subject to availability of funding.
During the online degree application, applicants can indicate their wish to apply for this scholarship. Should you wish to apply for the scholarship, please explain, in less than 500 words, why you are more preferable to receive the scholarship.
Name : Research Assistantships & Teaching Assistantships by Department Advisors
Amount : The amounts may vary with contribution and devoted hours. Please consult with academic advisors for further details.
Additional notes : Depending on research and teaching needs and advisees' academic performance, Department advisors may provide TA ships or RA ships.
Students apply automatically with their application for the degree programs; there is no other document required.
Scholarship from NTU
Please refer to NTU Overseas Student Admissions >> Apply - Degree & Non-Degree Admissions >> Scholarships - Degree Admissions for detailed information.
*International student applicants who apply through the TIGP system are only eligible for TIGP scholarships, and are not able to receive the NTU scholarships.
